text.p: These are the headlines for selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ottawa offers immigration deal: Ontario, B.C., Alberta being wooed with expanded control, more cash to ease grievances.
- Tycoon seeking to save Serbia: Ex-Milosevic ally has Canadian ties.
- Parents quit suit against Red Cross: Charity's legal tactics criticized.
- Papal advance troops woo cynical Cubans: It's an uphill task. Forty foreign priests already are telling the people about the pontiff.
- Overnight guests new problem for Clinton: President's note on pursuing donors with promises of stays in Lincoln Bedroom called 'smoking gun.'
- Greenspan shocks markets: Dow and TSE sink on renewed warning about overheated trading.
- Canadian Air posts hefty loss: Executives optimistic, observers cautious after red ink flows again in '96.
- Hollinger unit's profit soars: Publisher says it's finding new ways to cut costs at Southam.
- Quebec loan plan gives undertakers a new lease on life: Co-ops want dying to remain a distinct experience.
- Greenspan warning hits stocks, bonds: Federal Reserve chief voices concern over 'excessive optimism,' inflationary pressure.
- Canadian Airlines Corp flies into negative equity with C$187-million loss.
